Wireless Phone Microphone: The small receiver plugs into a phone’s charging port, and the clip-on transmitter is worn near the collar. Most pair by themselves when switched on. Check that the receiver’s plug matches your phone.
AKAI Drum Pad: A pad controller for finger drumming.
LIVID Alias 8: Eight channel faders and a master fader, sixteen knobs, sixteen buttons and one push dial. Made for mixing and controlling software such as Ableton Live.
USB Speakers: These take power from a USB port. Some also take their sound through USB, in which case choose them as the output in sound settings; others still need the 3.5 mm plug in the headphone socket.
Fostex 6301 Powered Speakers: Small studio monitors. Each one is a single mono speaker with a volume knob on the front and a 1/4 inch input on the back. For stereo, send left to one and right to the other.
Desktop Microphone Stand: A short stand for a table, for podcasts and video calls.
Multi-Function Stand: Check what the top fitting takes before you borrow it: a mic thread, a tablet holder or a small light.
Backlight Base: A low floor base for placing a light close to the ground, for example behind a subject to light the background or their outline.
USB DVD DRIVE: Reads CDs and DVDs. It cannot read Blu-ray discs.
USB BluRay Drive: Reads Blu-ray, DVD and CD. Playing a Blu-ray movie needs player software that supports it; neither Windows nor macOS can do it on their own.
Magnus VT-4000 Tripod: A video tripod. Its fluid head moves with smooth resistance for pans and tilts, with separate pan and tilt locks and a long handle.
Compact Action Tripod: A light travel tripod for small cameras, action cameras and phones.
GorillaPod 1K Flexible Mini-Tripod with: Made for up to 1 kg (2.2 lb): a compact camera, small mirrorless camera or phone.
GorillaPod SLR-Zoom Flexible Mini- Tripo: Made for up to 3 kg (6.6 lb): a DSLR with a zoom lens.
Mini Flex Tripod B: Check the weight it is made for before trusting a camera to it.
10-18mm Ultra Wide-Angle Contemporary Le: Sony E-mount. A very wide zoom for interiors, landscapes, architecture and filming yourself at arm’s length. Keep the camera level to stop walls leaning.
4mm f/2.8 Circular Fisheye Lens (Sony E-: Sony E-mount. Sees about half a sphere and records it as a circle in the middle of the frame, with black corners. Most lenses of this kind are manual: set focus and the f-number on the lens. Your feet and tripod legs easily get into the picture.
Canon EF 75mm-300mm f/4-5.6 Lens: Canon EF mount (Canon DSLRs). A telephoto zoom for sports, wildlife and distant detail. Most versions have no stabiliser, so use a fast shutter speed, about 1/500 at the long end, or a tripod.
Canon Macro Lens EF 100mm f/2.8: Canon EF mount. A macro lens that focuses close enough to show a small object at life size on the sensor. A switch limits the focus range to speed up autofocus. Also a good portrait lens.
Laowa Sony A 60mm f/2.8 Lens: Sony A-mount; it needs the A-mount to E-mount adapter to fit a Sony mirrorless camera. A manual macro lens that can magnify up to twice life size. Set focus and the f-number on the lens, and use a tripod.
Micro-NIKKOR 55mm f/2.8 Lens: Nikon F mount. A classic manual-focus close-up lens, known for sharpness. It reaches half life size on its own. Set the f-number with the ring on the lens.
Panasonic Lumix Vario 12-35mm f/2.8 II L: Micro Four Thirds mount (Panasonic Lumix G, Olympus/OM System, some Blackmagic cameras). An everyday zoom from wide to short portrait that keeps f/2.8 through the whole range.
Sony E 30mm f/3.5 Macro Lens: Sony E-mount. A small autofocus macro lens that reaches life size, with the subject only a few centimetres from the front of the lens. Take the hood off so it does not shade the subject.
Tilt 50mm F1.4 Lens (Sony E-mount): Sony E-mount, manual focus. The front of the lens tilts, which slants the band of sharp focus across the picture. Use it for the miniature-scene look or to keep one slice sharp. Focus after you tilt.
Tokina AT-X124 Wide-Angle AF PRO DX II 1: A wide zoom for DSLRs with the smaller APS-C sensor, sold in Canon and Nikon mounts; check which this one is. Pull the focus ring back toward the camera for hand focus and push it forward for autofocus.
